body.objective: Decide the reconstruction status of the positive Bateman--Turok Euclidean lattice at finite volume and prove or obstruct the first actual volume-uniform interacting estimate needed for a continuum limit, while keeping positive-Hilbert, Krein, Born, continuum-identification, and Lorentzian claims as distinct gates.
activates: a volume-normalized half-action-density low-mode curvature theorem or obstruction
a certified affine radial-virial theorem and actual uniform Gibbs action-density estimate
an actual interacting H^-1 moment theorem or a diverging-volume counterexample
tightness in an explicitly weaker negative-Sobolev topology only after the moment theorem
a refinement-stable ordinary-OS disposition separate from an indefinite-metric reconstruction gate
a weak-base dependency DAG for the first finite-to-continuum analytic bridge
body.current_gate: The affine theorem D>=2A-(488/5)N now proves the actual volume-uniform Gibbs action density and E[sqrt(1+A/N)] bound at lambda=0.4. Next prove or obstruct positivity/invertibility of the orthogonal Hessian block required to define the lowest-mode Schur complement globally, then test with exact algebra and bounded adversarial searches whether (kappa_h(psi)/kappa_h(0))*sqrt(1+A(psi)/N) has a positive volume-independent lower bound. If either curvature gate fails, pass to an independently normalized low-mode marginal. No action-density or method theorem counts as the actual H^-1 moment.
body.stop_condition: EITHER prove an actual volume-uniform interacting H^-1 second-moment bound and identify the resulting tightness topology, with an independently verified certificate; OR exhibit an exact or rigorously controlled volume sequence on which that actual moment diverges, thereby obstructing the estimate itself. The already certified finite-volume ordinary-OS obstructions must remain explicit, and neither branch may be promoted to continuum identification, Born probability, Krein reconstruction, or Lorentzian physics without separate bridge certificates.
body.forbid: no finite-volume OS failure called a continuum OS theorem; no pointwise curvature, Brascamp--Lieb, Schwinger--Dyson-sign, virial, sampler, or reference-measure method obstruction called failure of the actual Gibbs moment; no H^-1 bound called tightness in H^-1 rather than in a declared compactly weaker topology; no subsequential tightness called limit identification; no positive Euclidean Gibbs measure called a Born rule; no ordinary-OS obstruction called a Krein no-go; no EUCLIDEAN-SPECTRAL or REDUCED-MODE evidence used for LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL claims
body.resource_hint: Run all computations sequentially under ulimit -v 500000. Normalize action by N before proposing an annealed half weight. The exact period-three family forces pointwise weight exponent p>=1/2. The homogeneous coefficient-two virial inequality fails, but the affine volume-defect theorem already bounds the actual annealed half-action factor; do not redo that gate. If a uniform H^-1 bound is proved, use the compact embedding H^-1 into H^(-1-epsilon) for tightness and keep limit identification separate.
